title: There is no theory for extrapolating successful replication of selected trials to new questions
statement: Agreement between an emulation and a randomized trial raises confidence, and disagreement can arise from emulation failure, random error, different adherence, different measurement, different populations, or a limitation of the trial itself. RCT-DUPLICATE and the 2026 concordance meta-analysis both show better agreement under closer emulation and neither shows equivalence: across 107 paired emulations and trials the effect correlation was 0.59 overall and 0.83 among the 63 pairs judged to emulate more closely. What no one has is a theory that licenses the inference from those results to a new question: how much confidence a successful replication of trial A in database D transfers to question B in database D, or to question A in database E. Publishing after the trial result is known also creates design-calibration and selective-reporting risks that the concordance statistic cannot see.
why_open: The benchmarking set is not a random sample of questions: trials get emulated when they are recent, large, and have an accessible active comparator, which are the conditions under which emulation works best. A concordance statistic is therefore an estimate of performance on a favorable subpopulation, with no design that would identify performance elsewhere. Attributing a discrepancy requires knowing which of six candidate causes produced it, and the data that would separate them, particularly the trial's own adherence and measurement, are typically not available to the emulator.

prior_work.what_it_does: Pools 107 emulation-trial pairs, reporting correlation 0.59 overall and 0.83 among closer emulations, and links poorer concordance to baseline imbalance, hospital-initiated treatment and inferior outcome emulation.

proposed_direction: Run prospective, blinded benchmarking suites in which the emulation protocol and code are frozen and registered before the trial result is revealed, which removes design calibration by construction rather than by assurance. Model concordance hierarchically by data source, clinical setting, outcome type and degree of protocol match, so the quantity estimated is a conditional expectation of agreement rather than a global rate. Treat benchmarking as calibration evidence about a data source and a design class, never as certification of a method.
severity: Benchmarking results are cited as general warrant for emulation, and the inference from them to a new question has no support.

title: Replication is reported as a binary label rather than as a calibrated comparison of estimands
statement: Agreement between an emulation and a trial is informative only when the estimands, populations and measurements are close enough to be comparable, and better design alignment is empirically associated with stronger concordance. Benchmarking nonetheless reports success or failure as a binary label, usually derived from whether the confidence intervals overlap or whether the direction agrees. That label mixes estimand mismatch with random error: two studies estimating the same quantity with wide intervals will agree by that criterion, and two estimating different quantities precisely will disagree. The reported statistic therefore does not measure what its users take it to measure.
why_open: Constructing a graded measure requires deciding how much estimand difference is tolerable, which is a judgment the binary label exists to avoid. Prediction-interval coverage would be the natural criterion and requires a distributional claim about the trial's own error that the trial does not publish. The label is also convenient for the audiences who cite benchmarking results, so there is little pressure to replace it.

proposed_direction: Report the ratio of effects, the absolute effect difference, standardized agreement and prediction-interval coverage together, so that estimand mismatch and random error are separately visible. Use positive and negative controls alongside the trial comparison, and prefer prospective forecasts of a trial's result to retrospective comparisons, since only the former is uncontaminated by knowing the answer. Replicate across databases as well as across questions, because a data source's calibration is what a decision-maker actually needs to know.

title: Convergence of treatment in the comparator arm attenuates the observational intention-to-treat analogue with follow-up length
statement: The observational analogue of an intention-to-treat effect contrasts assigning initiation now against not initiating now. Two things then happen that do not happen in a randomized trial. Assignment is confounded, so the contrast requires baseline adjustment to mean anything. And the comparator group does not stay untreated: patients assigned to no initiation now frequently initiate later, so with longer follow-up the two strategies converge and the estimated effect attenuates toward the null for reasons that have nothing to do with the treatment's efficacy. The attenuation is a function of the follow-up horizon and of local prescribing behavior, and it is rarely reported as such, so an emulation with long follow-up and a null result cannot be distinguished from one where the treatment does not work.
why_open: The convergence is a real feature of the strategy contrast rather than a bias to be removed, so it cannot be adjusted away without changing to a per-protocol estimand that carries its own assumptions. Reporting it requires publishing the treatment trajectories in both arms over follow-up, which most papers do not, and the rate of convergence depends on the health system and calendar period rather than on anything intrinsic. There is also no convention for choosing the horizon at which the contrast is still meaningful.

title: Data-fitness assessment is narrative and has no thresholds that would stop a study
statement: Electronic health records arise from encounters, billing and documentation rather than from scheduled research assessments, so eligibility and follow-up in an emulation partly reflect care-seeking and access rather than the biology the protocol intends. Whether a given database can support a given target trial is therefore a question about the data source and the trial jointly. In practice this is answered narratively, in a paragraph asserting that the data are suitable, with no quantitative thresholds and no procedure that could return the answer no. A pipeline that cannot conclude that the trial is not emulable will always produce an estimate, and the estimate will not carry the fact that the question could not be asked.
why_open: Fitness is not a property of the data alone but of the pair formed by the data and the protocol, so a fixed score is the wrong object and a per-protocol assessment has to be constructed each time. Any threshold that would stop a study is a threshold that costs someone a publication, and no external body currently imposes one. There is also a measurement problem underneath: assessing capture continuity or outcome validity generally requires a validation source, and if that source existed the fitness question would be less pressing.

title: Averaging site estimates in a federated emulation can conceal that the sites emulated different trials
statement: Distributed health data improve power and support transportability, and patient-level sharing is often prohibited, which is why federated emulation has been proposed and demonstrated for distributed effect estimation. The statistical machinery for combining site estimates is not the hard part. The hard part is that sites differ in coding systems, treatment availability, confounding structure and time resolution, so the same executable protocol can define materially different eligibility, exposure and outcome at each site. Averaging the resulting estimates produces a number whose estimand is the average of several different questions, and nothing in the aggregation step detects that.
why_open: The incompatibility is semantic rather than statistical: two sites can both return well-estimated, internally valid effects for populations the protocol was not intended to distinguish, and no summary of the estimates reveals it. The diagnostics that would reveal it require the patient-level data that federation exists to keep local. Heterogeneity statistics cannot separate real effect modification from mapping failure, since both produce between-site variance.

title: Common data models harmonize structure without guaranteeing that the same variable means the same thing
statement: Claims, records, registries, mortality files and laboratory data each carry part of what a protocol needs, and linking them changes both who is eligible and which outcomes are captured. Linkage is imperfect and coding systems change over time, so the same analytic variable can shift meaning across sites and across years within a site. Multi-source linked databases are associated with better emulation of trials, which makes the linkage decisions consequential rather than administrative. Common data models solve the structural half of this and do not guarantee semantic or causal equivalence, and the historical code mappings and extract versions that would let a reader check are rarely preserved in publications.
why_open: Semantic drift is invisible in the analytic dataset: the column is populated and the values are in range. Detecting it requires the mapping history and a comparison across extracts, both of which are usually discarded once the analytic file is built. Linkage error is also non-random, correlating with the same social and health-system factors that predict treatment and outcome, so it is a confounded measurement error rather than noise.

title: An unrecorded eligibility criterion is indistinguishable from a criterion that was met
statement: Trial eligibility is assessed at a screening visit; a database records what a clinician happened to order. Restricting an emulation to patients with complete eligibility information therefore selects on laboratory testing, clinical documentation and specialist access, which differ systematically from the excluded patients. Weighting methods for missing eligibility have recently been developed and the literature remains small. The harder version of the problem is that eligibility is latent rather than merely missing: an absent creatinine value is consistent both with a patient who would have failed the criterion and with one who was never tested, and the missingness itself may depend on treatment anticipation or on the impending outcome.
why_open: Missing-at-random conditional on the recorded history is not credible here, because the recording decision is a clinical judgment informed by exactly the severity that predicts the outcome. Distinguishing latent eligibility from missing measurement requires a validation source in which the criterion was assessed for everyone, and such sources are rare and rarely representative. Imputing the value and imputing eligibility are different operations with different targets, and the literature has not separated them.

title: Eligibility criteria built from healthcare-use variables can induce selection through colliders
statement: An eligibility criterion is a conditioning statement, and conditioning on a variable that is a common effect of treatment and outcome opens a path rather than closing one. Emulation protocols routinely build eligibility from healthcare-use variables such as a required prior visit, a recorded baseline laboratory value or a minimum enrollment period, all of which can be descendants of the treatment decision or of early disease. Nothing in the current workflow checks an eligibility definition for this property, and the reporting checklist asks what the criteria were rather than what conditioning on them does.
why_open: Whether a criterion is a collider depends on the causal structure, which is what the study is trying to learn, so the check cannot be purely empirical. Graph-learning algorithms recover only a Markov equivalence class and are further limited by latent confounding, so they can flag candidates and cannot certify. Removing a criterion also changes the target population, which means the correction has a cost that must be argued clinically rather than statistically.

title: Emulation assumes no interference, and cloning individuals can produce joint strategies nobody could implement
statement: One person's treatment can change another's outcome through infection, provider behavior, household exposure or a shared resource constraint. Target trial emulation as normally practiced assumes this does not happen. Methods under partial interference define direct and spillover effects and are well developed in their own literature, but they are rarely joined to emulation, and the join is not cosmetic: eligibility, assignment and positivity all become cluster- or network-dependent quantities. Cloning individuals independently, which is the standard device for grace periods, can assign a set of clones a joint strategy that no cluster could actually receive, so the artificial censoring is then censoring on an impossible world. The TARGET reporting guideline currently offers no cluster-trial extension.
why_open: Under interference the estimand has to be defined through an exposure mapping, and there is no canonical mapping: own treatment plus treated-neighbor proportion is one choice among many and different choices give different, equally valid, effects. Positivity must hold for the joint neighborhood exposure, which is a far stronger requirement than individual positivity and typically fails in observed networks. Networks are also measured with error, and contagion, homophily and spillover are only weakly separable from one another even when the network is known exactly.

prior_work.what_it_does: Defines direct and spillover effects for cluster and population-level allocation, one of the frameworks that would have to be joined to the emulation protocol.

proposed_direction: Define network target trials in which the exposure mapping is part of the protocol rather than an analysis convenience, and state the positivity condition for the joint neighborhood exposure explicitly. Develop cluster-level clone-censor-weighting so that compatibility is judged for the cluster rather than the individual, alongside network targeted learning and agent-based g-computation. Test sensitivity to network mismeasurement and to violations of partial interference by deleting edges at known rates, because a method that is correct on a perfectly observed network and silent on a noisy one is not usable on real data.

title: Transporting an observational estimate compounds sampling assumptions on top of confounding assumptions with no accounting
statement: An internally valid estimate need not apply to the health system, population or calendar period where the decision will be made. Weighting, outcome modeling and doubly robust transport estimators all exist, and all of them require that the effect modifiers be measured, that the populations overlap, and that effects be conditionally exchangeable across samples. Applied transport work still mostly uses conventional sampling weights or outcome models despite the more flexible alternatives. The deeper issue is that transporting an observational estimate stacks the sampling-exchangeability assumption on top of the treatment-exchangeability assumption, and no current reporting practice shows how the two compound or which one a given discrepancy should be charged to.
why_open: Both assumption sets are untestable and they fail in correlated ways: a health system whose case mix differs is usually also one whose confounding structure and treatment availability differ, so a single sensitivity parameter cannot represent the joint failure. Unmeasured effect modification is not detectable in the source population, since by construction it is a variable nobody measured. Combining transport with flexible representation learning risks erasing the very effect modification that transport is supposed to preserve, because predictive invariance and causal invariance are different properties.

Derive bounds under unmeasured effect modification and report them alongside the point estimate, so a transported number carries its own fragility. title: A hazard ratio is reported where the estimand was a weighted per-protocol effect among the grace-period compatible
statement: Hazard ratios, odds ratios and model coefficients are routinely presented without naming the intervention, the population, the time horizon or the strategy for each intercurrent event. title: Cross-validation for longitudinal nuisance models optimizes prediction, not causal performance
statement: Marginal structural models, the parametric g-formula, g-estimation and longitudinal targeted learning all identify sustained-regime effects under sequential exchangeability and positivity, and all of them require nuisance models for treatment, censoring and outcome. When those nuisance models are fitted by machine learning, the model that predicts treatment best is not the model that produces the best causal estimate: a highly adaptive learner can achieve excellent discrimination while returning near-zero treatment probabilities, poor longitudinal balance and invalid inference. Standard cross-validation selects on prediction loss and is blind to all three. No selection criterion in routine use combines treatment prediction with longitudinal balance, weight dispersion and an estimate of the influence-function remainder, and no default library is tuned for the causal objective rather than the predictive one.
why_open: The causal loss is not computable from the data the way a predictive loss is: the counterfactual contrast the estimator targets is never observed, so the quantity one would like to cross-validate against does not exist as a label. Balance and weight-dispersion criteria are computable but are not losses in the decision-theoretic sense and can be optimized by learners that fit poorly. Sequential double robustness is proved under conditions that do not obviously hold when the observation process in electronic health records is itself informative, so the theory that would justify a criterion is incomplete precisely where the data are hardest.

title: Identification of dynamic regimes in continuous time under treatment-dependent observation is unresolved
statement: Treatments, outcomes and clinical observations occur asynchronously and are recorded at times determined by the care process. Almost every applied g-method assumes a prespecified discrete grid, and discretization can reverse temporal ordering between a treatment and an outcome that fell in the same interval, merge multiple events into one, or define an estimand that exists only relative to the chosen interval. General identification results for dynamic regimes under irregular observation, treatment-dependent visiting and within-interval effects remain limited, so the applied analyst working in continuous time has a modeling apparatus without an identification theorem to sit under it.
why_open: In continuous time the treatment process, the visit process and the outcome process are counting processes whose intensities depend on each other, and sequential exchangeability has to be stated with respect to filtrations rather than to a fixed sequence of covariate vectors. The conditions under which a dynamic regime is identified in that setting are strictly stronger and harder to interpret than their discrete counterparts. There is also no natural sample-size asymptotics: the information about an intensity comes from event counts rather than from patients, so the usual scaling arguments do not apply cleanly.

title: Large databases yield small effective samples after eligibility, comparator restriction and weighting
statement: A database of millions can carry very little information about a specific target trial once strict eligibility, active-comparator restriction and weighting have been applied, and extreme weights reduce the effective sample size much further than the nominal count suggests. Conventional asymptotic inference then becomes unreliable, most sharply for rare competing events and for subgroup effects, which are precisely the quantities decision-makers ask about. Papers continue to report the nominal number of patients, which for a weighted longitudinal analysis is not the quantity that governs the variance.

title: Emulation is proposed for non-pharmaceutical and policy interventions whose treatment versions and assignment units are not defined
statement: Interference, combination therapies, multiple treatment versions and non-pharmaceutical interventions all violate the two-arm, individually assigned, well-defined-intervention assumptions that the standard emulation protocol makes. What is missing is a statement of which protocol components a policy intervention can actually satisfy and what estimand results when several cannot.

The assignment unit for a policy is usually a jurisdiction, which reduces the effective sample to the number of jurisdictions and makes the analysis a small-n problem regardless of how many patients it contains. Version variation is intrinsic to implementation rather than incidental, so the consistency assumption fails by construction rather than by accident.

title: Regulators have no thresholds for adequate emulation, acceptable residual confounding or sufficient sensitivity analysis
statement: FDA guidance asks sponsors to describe an approach that supports causal inference and names target trial emulation where appropriate. NICE states that some target trials cannot be adequately emulated and that bespoke data collection may then be preferable. EMA and ICH guidance emphasize fit-for-use data, prespecification and transparent non-interventional design. What none of them supplies is a threshold: how close an emulation must be to count as adequate, how much residual confounding is acceptable for a given decision, or what set of sensitivity analyses is sufficient. Sponsors therefore cannot know in advance whether a submission will be accepted, and reviewers have no consistent basis on which to accept or reject one.

Any fixed threshold would be gamed and would also be wrong for some decisions, since the tolerable bias depends on what the decision costs. Agencies are also reasoning from a small and non-random set of precedents, so the empirical base for calibrating a threshold does not yet exist.

title: Calling an analysis a target trial emulation is treated as evidence about its assumption burden
statement: The assumptions an analysis needs form a ladder, and each step up adds one: from describing an association, to adjusting for measured confounders, to identifying a sustained-strategy effect, to transporting that effect to another population. A paper should identify the highest step its evidence plausibly reaches. In practice the label target trial emulation is doing that work instead: an analysis that adopts the framework is read as though it had climbed the ladder, when the framework secures the temporal alignment and nothing above it. The label has become a claim about credibility rather than a description of a design, and no convention exists for stating which step a given study actually reaches.
why_open: The framework's value is real, which is what makes the substitution durable: naming the target trial does prevent a class of self-inflicted biases, so the label is informative and is then over-read. There is no established vocabulary for the intermediate rungs, so an author wishing to be precise has to invent the terms. Reviewers and editors also use the label as a screening heuristic, which rewards using it and penalizes qualifying it.

title: Sequential emulation creates repeated participation and calendar-time confounding that its efficiency gain conceals
statement: Sequential emulation exploits repeated eligibility: a new trial is emulated at each decision point, and a person who is eligible at many points contributes to many trials. This uses the data better than a single baseline emulation and it introduces three complications together. The same person appears in many nested trials, so the observations are dependent in a way the pooled analysis must handle. Trials begun at different calendar times occur under different treatment availability, guidelines and background risk, so calendar time confounds the pooled contrast unless it is modeled. And a person's later eligibility is itself a consequence of earlier untreated survival, which links the trials causally rather than merely statistically. The efficiency gain is real and it is what makes these complications easy to overlook.
why_open: Pooling across trials requires an assumption that the effect is common across start times, which is exactly what calendar-time variation in practice makes doubtful, and testing it costs the efficiency the design was adopted for. The dependence is induced by the design rather than present in the data, so it has no natural clustering variable other than the person. Later eligibility conditional on earlier survival is a selection process, and whether it is innocuous depends on the outcome model being correct, which is the thing under test.

proposed_direction: Model calendar time explicitly as an effect modifier rather than adjusting it away, and report the trial-specific estimates alongside the pooled one so that a pooled effect resting on incompatible start times is visible. Derive variance estimators that account for repeated participation by the same person across nested trials, and check their coverage against a bootstrap over persons. Establish whether the efficiency gain survives the correct variance treatment, since the case for the design rests on a comparison that has usually been made under the naive variance.

title: Variance estimation after cloning and sequence expansion has no scalable, correct default
statement: Sequential emulation and cloning expand a dataset by orders of magnitude: each person contributes a row per eligible decision point, and cloning multiplies that by the number of strategies with which the person is initially compatible. Two dependence structures result. Repeated eligibility means a person appears in many trials, and cloning means several rows are copies of the same person's history. Naive standard errors ignore both. The bootstrap is correct in principle and often prohibitive at this scale, particularly with flexible nuisance models that must be refitted per replicate. The `TrialEmulation` package supports sequence expansion, censoring weights, outcome models and chunked processing, and general scalable variance estimation for this design remains unsettled.
why_open: The dependence is nested rather than simply clustered: clones within a person within a site, with the clone-level dependence induced by the analysis rather than present in the data. Influence-function variance estimators need the influence function of the full estimator including the weight-estimation step, which is not available in closed form once the nuisance models are learned. Every workaround trades in the same currency, since subsampling to make the bootstrap affordable reintroduces the finite-sample instability the bootstrap was there to characterize.

Support the scale with streaming risk-set construction, columnar back ends such as DuckDB or Arrow, sparse history representations, and case-control sampling with proven error control rather than heuristic subsampling. title: Generative models are evaluated on distributional fidelity and used for causal work
statement: Generative patient models would support privacy-preserving code development, power planning and method stress testing, and synthetic patient data have shown value as a benchmark environment. The evaluation practice does not match the use. A model optimized for marginal or temporal fidelity can reproduce every observed association while generating wrong counterfactuals, wrong overlap and wrong time ordering, because none of those quantities appears in the loss. Privacy mechanisms compound this by suppressing rare patterns, and rare patterns are often exactly the causally important ones. Synthetic data are not evidence about treatment effects unless the generating model is causally valid, and current benchmarks do not test whether it is.
why_open: Causal fidelity is not identifiable from the observed data the generator was trained on: two structural models that agree on every observational distribution can disagree on every interventional one. Evaluating it therefore requires a gold-standard structural model rather than a real dataset, which changes the object being validated. Privacy and causal fidelity are also in direct tension, since the mechanisms that protect rare individuals remove the rare strata that carry the overlap.

title: No procedure defines clinically defensible equivalence classes of treatment versions
statement: A per-protocol effect requires censoring at deviation and weighting for the informative censoring that censoring creates. Beneath that mechanics sits a question the mechanics assume away: what counts as the same treatment. Real treatments differ by dose, route, provider, formulation, combination and adherence pattern, and two regimens sharing a label may not satisfy consistency. Clone-censor-weight handles the case where baseline assignment is genuinely ambiguous, at the cost of data expansion, artificial censoring and sensitivity to the censoring model, but it takes the strategy definition as given. There is no guidance for constructing defensible equivalence classes of treatment versions, and none for overlapping combination therapies where a patient is simultaneously compatible with more than one labeled strategy.
why_open: Consistency is an assumption about the world rather than about the data, so no amount of data adjudicates whether two versions are the same treatment. The clinical judgment that would adjudicate it is specific to the drug, the indication and the era, which makes a general criterion the wrong shape for the problem. Making the versions explicit also multiplies the strategies, and each additional strategy costs positivity, so the honest specification is often the one the data cannot support.

title: No outcome-blind procedure selects the time grid or the grace period
statement: An emulated protocol has to fix three times that a randomized trial fixes in one act: when eligibility is assessed, when treatment is assigned, and when follow-up begins. It also has to fix the resolution at which time is measured, because routine data arrive as dated records rather than as a schedule of study visits. Clone-censor-weight and sequential emulation both handle the misalignment itself, but neither chooses the grace period or the interval width, and estimates move with both. A coarse interval lets treatment affect an outcome inside the interval before censoring is applied; a fine interval produces high-dimensional nuisance models and unstable weights. What does not exist is a procedure that selects either quantity from the treatment and observation processes alone, without touching outcome information, together with a reported measure of how far the estimate would have moved under the alternatives.
why_open: The choice is made before any model is fitted, so no model can price it. Selecting the grid or the grace period by fit to the outcome is the one move that would turn it into a statistical problem, and it is exactly the move that induces selection. The clinically meaningful interval is a property of the disease and of the care process rather than of the data, and no purely data-driven criterion recovers it. Published emulations overwhelmingly report a single specification, so the field also lacks the empirical distribution of how much the answer depends on it.

title: Negative controls, proxies and validation data are not integrated into a standard emulation workflow
statement: Specifying a target trial prevents the temporal biases an analyst inflicts on themselves; it does not create randomization. Active-comparator new-user designs, high-dimensional propensity scores and richer clinical measurements all reduce residual confounding without guaranteeing exchangeability. The tools that address what remains, negative control outcomes and exposures, instrumental variables, proximal causal learning and external validation samples, exist separately and are not part of any standard emulation workflow: there is no agreed order in which to apply them, no convention for reporting what each one bought, and no accepted way to combine their answers when they disagree. Covariate balance continues to be reported as though it bore on unmeasured confounding, which it does not.
why_open: Each of these tools identifies under assumptions that are themselves untestable and that differ from one another, so combining them is not a matter of adding evidence but of reconciling incompatible identification stories. A negative control shares only some of the confounding mechanisms of the primary outcome, and how much is not knowable from the data. Proximal methods need proxies satisfying completeness-type conditions that cannot be checked, and weak proxies produce unstable estimates that look like precision loss rather than assumption failure. Validation subsamples are rarely random, which imports a second selection problem into the correction for the first.

title: Sensitivity analyses vary one violated assumption at a time when several are violated together
statement: A conventional emulation reports a point estimate under exchangeability, positivity and correct measurement, and then a sensitivity analysis that relaxes one of them. In a longitudinal emulation on routine data all of them are doubtful simultaneously: unmeasured confounding, selection into the cohort, misclassification of exposure and outcome, and practical positivity failure all operate at once and interact. There is little theory for the joint case, so the reported uncertainty is a sampling interval around a point that is identified only under a conjunction the analysis has already conceded is false. What is missing is a way to report an identification region reflecting all the violations together, separately from the sampling interval.
why_open: Bias parameters for different violations live on different scales and enter the estimating equations at different places, so there is no natural single-parameter family to sweep. The joint region is typically not a product of the marginal regions because the violations interact, which means the computationally convenient answer is also the wrong one. Reporting a wide identification region is also professionally costly: it makes an honest analysis look weaker than a naive one, and no journal currently requires it.
